🧬 Plus Two Zoology Christmas Exam 2026 – Griffith's Experiment | Important Question Discussion | Molecular Basis of Inheritance | Kerala Class 12 Biology

Attention Kerala Plus Two Zoology students! Are you preparing for the upcoming Plus Two Christmas Exam 2026? Don't miss this important question discussion on Griffith's Experiment, a fundamental topic from the chapter Molecular Basis of Inheritance! 💯

In this RK Nex Plus Two session, we explain Frederick Griffith's Transformation Experiment (1928), its observations, conclusions, and significance in understanding the genetic material.

Learn how Griffith demonstrated bacterial transformation using Streptococcus pneumoniae, why the experiment was important, and how to write clear, examination-oriented answers.

📌 In This Video:

✅ Plus Two Zoology Christmas Exam 2026
✅ Griffith's Experiment – Important Question
✅ Molecular Basis of Inheritance
✅ Frederick Griffith's Experiment (1928)
✅ Bacterial Transformation Experiment
✅ Streptococcus pneumoniae
✅ Smooth Strain (S Strain)
✅ Rough Strain (R Strain)
✅ Virulent and Non-Virulent Bacteria
✅ Live S Strain – Experimental Observation
✅ Live R Strain – Experimental Observation
✅ Heat-Killed S Strain
✅ Heat-Killed S Strain + Live R Strain
✅ Discovery of the Transforming Principle
✅ Griffith's Experiment – Results
✅ Griffith's Experiment – Conclusion
✅ Significance of Bacterial Transformation
✅ Avery, MacLeod and McCarty's Experiment
✅ Important Diagram-Based Questions
✅ Christmas Exam Answer-Writing Tips

🎯 Why Watch This Video?

Griffith's Experiment (1928) is a fundamental topic in the chapter Molecular Basis of Inheritance. It introduced the concept of bacterial transformation and contributed to the discovery of DNA as genetic material.

Griffith demonstrated that a transforming principle from heat-killed S-strain bacteria could convert living R-strain bacteria into virulent S-strain bacteria. However, Griffith himself did not identify the transforming principle as DNA. That was established through later experiments by Avery, MacLeod, and McCarty. 
NCERT


This video helps students understand the experiment, remember its observations, and prepare clear, examination-oriented answers.

💯 Understand the Experiment. Remember the Observations. Aim for A+!
